mcu_block.name: RP2040 + CAN block
mcu_block.summary: Every Talos board uses the same copy-pasted Altium device sheet: an RP2040, 16 MB flash, a 12 MHz crystal, a Tag-Connect SWD pad, reset/boot buttons, an RGB status LED, and an MCP2517FD SPI CAN FD controller with a TJA1442 transceiver and a slide switch for the 120 ohm termination (2 x 60.4 ohm, split).

parts.role: CAN termination on/off ("TERM ON" on the silk)

firmware_facts.text: The RP2040 makes a 4 MHz clock from its 48 MHz USB clock on GPIO21 and feeds it to the MCP2517FD, which multiplies it by 10 to 40 MHz. SPI runs at 20 MHz.
Pin map shared by every board: CAN controller on SPI0 (nCS 17, SCK 18, MOSI 19, MISO 20), clock out on 21, interrupt on 22, status LED on 13/14/15, debug UART TX on 16.
The termination switch state is read back through the controller (MCP2517FD_TERM_SENSE_ON_INT0).

mcu_block.why: Mark 1 had I2C trouble over long wires (a 3 ft run to the depth sensor). Mark 2 put an RP2040 on every board and joined them with CAN instead of a shared I2C bus (story in the comments of tools/DeviceList.jsonc).

boards.name: POAC board
boards.status_basis: confirmed: talos/PoacBoard firmware, DeviceList "Talos Poactuator Board", pretest_checks expects it at bus 1 id 1
boards.location: board stack (the port-side electronics housing holds the board stack, per the 2024 team website)
boards.purpose: Takes both batteries, ORs them into one bus, makes the 15 V, 5 V, 12 V and 3.3 V rails, switches thruster power with the kill switch, measures the rails, and drives the torpedo/marker servo.
boards.why: Combines the Mark 2 power board and actuator board into one board to free space in the housing (team website). It keeps the power board's CAN ID 1, so software that looks for "the power board" still finds it.

key_ics.role: 15 V rail. Non-isolated DC-DC module, 9-53 V in, 3.3-15 V out, 20 A (trim R12 = 1.24 k)
5 V rail, same module (trim R13 = 8.56 k)
3 A LDO, 15 V -> 12 V for the servo output
800 mA LDO, 5 V -> 3.3 V for the RP2040 block
ideal-diode OR controllers: port and starboard battery onto V+ ("battery balancer" on the schematic)
Schottky diode, V+ -> Vreg (the regulators' input)
analog switch: the RP2040 SOFTWARE_KILL line can break the kill switch signal
3.3 V <-> 5 V level shifter for the servo data line

facts.text: Reads the physical kill switch on GPIO1 (interrupt on both edges) and drives SOFTWARE_KILL on GPIO2. GPIO2 starts in the kill state before safety is up.
Publishes state/kill every 150 ms and state/electrical every 1 s.

state/electrical: three_volt (ADC ch1, 10k/10k divider), balanced (ch2 = Vreg, 10k/1k), twelve_volt (ch3, which is wired to the 15 V rail), five_volt (ch4); port/stbd_powering from the LTC4412 STAT pins. port_voltage and stbd_voltage are sent as 0.
Turns the fan on at boot; command/electrical ENABLE_FANS / DISABLE_FANS switches it.

Drives one Hiwonder bus servo (half-duplex UART at 115200 baud from a PIO state machine on GPIO27) that indexes 2 torpedoes (240 and 200 deg) and 2 markers (0 and 50 deg). Firing is refused while killed or not armed.

revision.notes: Project PCB is PoactuatorPCB4 (ECO logs Jan 2024; PDF in the 2023-24 board-order release, Feb 2024). Last commit 2026-02-18: "poactuator fix to create separate output for servo 12V". Project title/revision fields are still the template placeholders, so no revision number.

boards.name: ESC board
boards.status_basis: confirmed: talos/ESCBoard firmware, CAN IDs 2 and 3, pretest_checks expects both
boards.purpose: Carries four APD 80F3 ESCs and talks to them with bidirectional DShot. Two identical boards drive the 8 thrusters.
boards.why: Bidirectional DShot gives RPM feedback on the same wire as the command. The APD firmware had no 3D (reversible) DShot mode, so the team patched the ESC firmware to add it.

key_ics.role: brushless ESC, 15-35 V, 80 A (schematic part description)
15 A fast fuse, one per ESC
60 A fuse on the board input
VCC_MEAS: thruster supply voltage into the RP2040 ADC

connectors.label: FLASH CONN
connectors.carries: 5V, RX, TX, GND to each ESC (for the APD configurator)

connectors.label: breakout
connectors.carries: PWM (DShot) and telemetry lines of all four ESCs

facts.text: DShot600, bidirectional, from PIO0; ESC UART telemetry read by PIO1.
Thrusters are held off for 5 s after ESC power appears (ESC_POWERUP_DELAY_MS 5000).
If no new RPM command arrives within 500 ms the thrusters stop, and stay off for 1 s.
ESC power counts as on above 9 V on VCC_MEAS.
Core 1 runs the RPM controller; disabled_flags explain why it is off: SAFETY_KILLED, ESC_BOARD_OFF, ESC_POWERON_DELAY, TGT_RPM_STALE, TGT_RPM_STALE_PENALTY, CONTROLLER_UNCONFIGURED.
The board reads the ID jumper on GPIO29 at boot: 0 -> CAN client 2, 1 -> CAN client 3.
Uses 7 pole pairs to turn electrical RPM into shaft RPM.

revision.notes: Designed for Tempest Mark 2 (Jan 2023) and reused on Talos. The repo has later edits (Oct-Dec 2025: "ESC Voltage protector", traces); unconfirmed whether the boards in Talos were rebuilt.

boards.name: Camera cage breakout board
boards.status_basis: confirmed: talos/CameraCageBB firmware, CAN ID 4, pretest_checks expects it
boards.location: camera cage (the computer side, with the Orin)
boards.purpose: Power and I/O hub of the camera cage: switches Orin power, reads the depth sensor, runs fans and the RGB status strip, injects power into the DVL Ethernet cable, and joins the Orin to both CAN buses.

key_ics.role: reverse-polarity protection on the 15 V input

connectors.label: ORIN CAN
connectors.carries: external CAN H/L, GND, internal CAN H/L (to the Orin)

connectors.label: DVL SUBCONN
connectors.carries: DVL Ethernet pairs + 15V/GND on pins 7-8 ("Ethernet Power Injection")

connectors.label: DVL | SWITCH
connectors.carries: the same Ethernet pairs, on to the network switch (no power)

connectors.label: SWITCH
connectors.carries: 5V for the network switch ("Network Switch Power")

facts.text: Reads the depth sensor as an MS5837-02BA on I2C (200 kHz) and publishes state/depth/raw in frame talos/pressure_link.
Turns the Orin switch and the fans on at boot.
Drives the RGB status strip from PIO0; command/led messages with the CCB target bit set it.
Still creates a state/leak publisher, but its periodic publish is commented out. The team no longer uses the leak sensor.

links: Bridges both CAN buses to the Orin (J10)

revision.notes: Mark 2 design (Jan 2023). Last commit 2024-11-10 "Added connectors and LDOs".

boards.name: LED board
boards.status_basis: confirmed: talos/LEDBoard firmware, CAN ID 6, pretest_checks expects it. The Year One design matches the firmware pin map (2 drivers, CONN_CHK, TEMP_SENSE); the Year Two LED_Board (5 drivers + analog mux) is not supported by the current firmware.
boards.purpose: Drives the vehicle light (an RGBW LED module) with two buck LED drivers; used for status signalling.

key_ics.role: SPI-controlled buck LED drivers (1.5 A), 2 channels each = R, G, B, W

connectors.label: LED module
connectors.carries: R/G/B/W anodes, GND, Temp_Sense (NTC), Conn CHK

inputs: V+ and 5V from the stack link
feeds: LED module (from V+ through the drivers)

facts.text: Subscribes to state/depth/raw and scales brightness with depth; also has temperature protection (commit history, Oct-Nov 2024).
Peak current set to 45 (driver register units, "see LED controller datasheet").

revision.notes: Year One (2023-24) design; template placeholders for title/revision. A Year Two redesign (TalosBoards/Year Two/LED_Board, 5 drivers) exists in the repo.

boards.name: LED module (aluminium)
boards.status_basis: inferred: in the 2023-24 Talos board-order release next to the LED board; the LED board connector carries R/G/B/W + an NTC like this module
boards.purpose: Aluminium-core LED board with four RGBW LEDs and a 22 k NTC thermistor, driven by the LED board.

boards.name: IVC board
boards.status_basis: confirmed: talos/IVCBoard firmware, CAN ID 8, DeviceList "Talos IVC Board", pretest_checks expects it
boards.purpose: Acoustic modem for talking to the second vehicle: drives a transducer and listens on a hydrophone. Also has a Bluetooth audio module that can play sound through the transducer.

key_ics.role: isolated DC-DC, V+ -> +/-24 V for the power amplifier (fused 1.5 A, F1)
isolated 5 V -> +/-5 V for the receive chain
selects RP2040 signal or Bluetooth audio for transmit

inputs: V+ and 5V from the stack link

facts.text: Two-tone FSK: 17 kHz and 19 kHz, 50 ms per symbol; packets are 8 data bits + a 4-bit CRC.
Receive uses an FFT (kiss FFT) on the ADC samples.
Schematic note: "Populate SB5 0 ohm for Lil' Boat, DNP for Talos". The firmware picks its Talos thresholds when GPIO6 (BOARD_ID_PIN) reads low.

revision.notes: Designed Mar-Apr 2025 ("ivc board ready to go out confirmed" 2025-03-19, "fixed opa548 lead mix-up" 2025-04-06).

boards.name: Smart battery housing MCU board
boards.status_basis: confirmed: talos/SmartBattery firmware; pretest_checks expects two housings on the external bus when running on batteries
boards.location: inside each battery housing (port and starboard)
boards.purpose: Reads the battery management chip, shows status on a small OLED, and reports the pack over the external CAN bus.

key_ics.role: soft power latch: reed switch, PWR_CTRL (MCU holds itself on) or PACK_PWR turns the board on
magnet-operated power button through the sealed housing

connectors.label: to BMS board
connectors.carries: CANL, CANH, BMS SCL/SDA, BMS_WAKE, GND, PACK_PWR, VBAT

facts.text: Talks SMBus to the BQ40Z80 from a PIO state machine (the BMS I2C pins are swapped relative to the RP2040 pin mux).
Its CAN client ID is the housing serial number stored in flash at 0x101FF000 (housings #1-#5 in DeviceList), not the PORT/STBD constants; port vs starboard is reported in BatteryStatus.detect.
Switches itself off when the pack is idle and the display is off.
The leak-triggered emergency power cut is commented out ("once leak false positives are fixed").

can.id_name: CANMORE_CLIENT_ID_SMART_BATERY_PORT / STBD are defined but not used by this firmware

boards.name: Smart battery housing BMS board
boards.status_basis: confirmed as the partner of the SBH MCU board (SmartBattery firmware reads a BQ40Z80)
boards.purpose: Battery management: cell monitoring and balancing, protection FETs, a 45 A protector fuse and the pack terminals.

connectors.label: external
connectors.carries: CAN H/L, Pack- , Pack+ (5 A fuse), Side_Detection, Detect

battery.note: Values from the BQ40Z80 gas-gauge config file in the repo; unconfirmed that every pack runs exactly this file. The same file lists Design Capacity 2000 mAh, which may be a placeholder.

revision.notes: Updated 2026-02-15 ("previous versions did the current calculation slightly wrong").

boards.name: Jetson AGX breakout
boards.status_basis: inferred: the team website lists a "CAN breakout board" on the Orin; this is the only Orin 40-pin board with two CAN transceivers. Software opens the IMU on /dev/ttyTHS0 and the CAN agent on can0.
boards.purpose: Adds CAN transceivers for the Orin's two built-in CAN controllers (can0, can1) and an RS-232 port for the VectorNav IMU.

key_ics.role: CAN transceivers for can1 and can0, each with a termination switch

revision.notes: Latest commit 2026-09-24: "Deleted NMOS components so that pin 1 on J2 is always at 5V" (IMU power no longer switched).

boards.name: Jetson AGX M.2 RS-422 card
boards.status_basis: inferred: the team website lists an "RS 422 breakout board (Fiber Optic Gyro interface)"; this M.2 card carries an RS-422 transceiver and a commit calls it the "FOG board". The gyro config uses /dev/ttyTHS2.
boards.purpose: Gives the Orin an RS-422 serial port and a 5 V supply for the fibre-optic gyro.

key_ics.role: LDO, 8 V -> 5 V for the gyro
1.8 V LDO for the transceiver logic side

revision.notes: 2024-10-06 "Revert FOG board changes since it works as-is"; Nov-Dec 2025 commits add an SPI-to-RS422 variant (work in progress).

boards.name: Mark 2 power board (retired)
boards.status_basis: replaced by the POAC board (same CAN ID 1; talos/PowerBoard firmware still in the repo)
boards.purpose: Original Mark 2 power distribution: battery ORing, 15 V/5 V regulators, kill switch.

boards.name: Mark 2 actuator board (retired)
boards.status_basis: its jobs moved to the POAC board; talos/Actuator firmware (CAN ID 5) still in the repo
boards.purpose: Old actuator board: claw motor driver (DRV8801), coil-gun style torpedo charging, droppers.
